landing.heroHeadline: Discover and share the best fly fishing spots
landing.heroSubheadline: Save locations, upload your catches, and explore spots shared by other anglers
landing.heroTagline: Fly fishing is much more than a sport. It's reading the river, interpreting the hatches, choosing the right fly. It's connecting with nature — an art passed down through generations of passionate anglers.
landing.builtByFishers:
Built for fly fishers,
by fly fishers
landing.missionDesc: Fly fishing has a deep history in Italy. From the alpine streams of Valtellina to the spring creeks of Friuli, from Val Camonica to the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines, every river has its soul and its secrets. Flywaters was born to collect this knowledge and make it available to all Italian fly fishers — from beginners to expert tyers. A no-kill community where you can share spots, techniques, patterns and catches with respect for fish and the environment.
landing.discoverSpotsDesc: Find the best Italian rivers and streams for fly fishing. Read reviews from anglers who fished there, discover the species present, the best season and water conditions. From the marble trout of the Sesia to the grayling of the Brenta, every spot has its story.
landing.shareCatchesDesc: Post your fishing photos, tag the spot, indicate the technique and fly used. Contribute to the collective knowledge of the community. Every documented catch is valuable data for all anglers who will come after you.
landing.connectCommunityDesc: Get in touch with fly fishers from all over Italy. Exchange tips on patterns, mayfly and caddis hatches, river conditions. Organize trips, find fishing buddies, learn from the most experienced.
landing.noKillDesc: No-kill is not just a rule — it's respect for the fish and the river. Every marble trout released is a trout that will grow again, that will return upstream, that another angler may encounter. On Flywaters, no-kill is a founding value: every photographed catch returns free to the water. Because the real trophy is not the fish — it's the moment.
landing.step1Desc: Create your profile in seconds. Choose your preferred fishing style — dry fly, nymph, streamer or tenkara — and start exploring right away.
landing.step2Desc: Navigate the interactive map of Italian spots. Filter by water type, target species and community rating. Every spot has photos, reviews and access information.
landing.step3Desc: Post your outings, review the spots you visited and message other anglers. Your experience enriches the entire community.

seasons.winterDesc: Snow-covered alpine streams, brown trout and grayling in crystal-clear waters. You'll need warm layers and sturdy waders.
seasons.springDesc: The season of hatches. Rivers in full flow, green meadows and the first dry flies of the year.
seasons.summerDesc: Golden lakes at sunset, long sessions with light gear. The perfect time to explore.
seasons.autumnDesc: Golden foliage along the streams, low and clear waters. The season of spawning char and the last hatches before winter.

brownTrout.name: Brown Trout
brownTrout.desc: The most common trout in Italian rivers. Responds well to dry fly during spring hatches.

marbleTrout.name: Marble Trout
marbleTrout.desc: Endemic to the Po basin. Can exceed 10kg, it is the most coveted catch for Italian fly fishers.

rainbowTrout.name: Rainbow Trout
rainbowTrout.desc: Introduced from North America, it is the ideal species for those starting fly fishing.

grayling.name: Grayling
grayling.desc: The dry fly fish par excellence. Its explosive surface rises are unforgettable.

brookTrout.name: Brook Trout
brookTrout.desc: Lives in the coldest and cleanest Alpine waters. Extraordinary colors, powerful fight.

arcticChar.name: Arctic Char
arcticChar.desc: Inhabitant of high-altitude Alpine lakes. Requires specific techniques and long hikes.

pike.name: Pike
pike.desc: The apex predator of Italian waters. Caught with large streamers.

chub.name: Chub
chub.desc: Often underestimated, the chub is an excellent dry fly fish during summer months.

barbel.name: Barbel
barbel.desc: Bottom-dwelling fish that responds well to heavy nymphs. Tenacious and resilient fighter.

carp.name: Carp
carp.desc: Sight fishing for carp is one of the most exciting fly fishing challenges in the lowlands.

entomology.label: ENTOMOLOGY
entomology.title: Know the insects, catch more fish
entomology.subtitle: Fly fishing is the art of imitating nature. Discover the insects that trigger rises.
entomology.ctaLead: Match the insects to the right flies — explore the spots

mayflies.name: Mayflies
mayflies.lifeCycle: The queens of dry fly fishing. Their hatches trigger the most spectacular rises. The life cycle lasts one to three years: aquatic nymph, sub-imago (dun) and flying imago (spinner) that lives only a few hours to reproduce.

caddisflies.name: Caddisflies
caddisflies.lifeCycle: Present year-round, they are the main food source for trout and grayling. Larvae build protective cases from pebbles or plant debris, then emerge as pupae and adults in mass on summer evenings.

stoneflies.name: Stoneflies
stoneflies.lifeCycle: Indicators of clean water. Their winter hatches are crucial for grayling. Nymphs live for up to three years under the rocks of well-oxygenated currents before crawling onto the bank to emerge.

trueFlies.name: True Flies
trueFlies.lifeCycle: Chironomids and simulids — often ignored but responsible for the most difficult rises. They hatch in large numbers on the surface, forcing fish into extreme selectivity on tiny imitations.

terrestrials.name: Terrestrials
terrestrials.lifeCycle: Ants, grasshoppers, caterpillars — fall into the water in summer and trigger sudden rises. They have no aquatic cycle but become protagonists during warm winds and summer storms.

dragonflies.name: Dragonflies
dragonflies.lifeCycle: Dragonfly nymphs are an important prey for pike and large trout. They live for up to two years on the bottom of lakes and still waters, actively preying on tadpoles and small fish.

beetles.name: Beetles
beetles.lifeCycle: Aquatic beetles are often overlooked but can trigger selective rises. They live both in water (diving beetles) and on land, ending up in rivers blown by wind or fallen from riparian vegetation.

alderflies.name: Alderflies
alderflies.lifeCycle: Their aquatic larvae are among the most imitated nymphs by fly tiers. They live for over a year in mud and among rocks, then emerge in spring as slow, clumsy-flying adults.
